steps.title: One family, two boot chains
steps.body: The two boards share the ROM-to-BL2-to-FIP design and the SD image rules, but they are built from different directories because the CPU architecture, toolchains and several boot components differ. The strips at the top show the stages; the table lists what is the same and what differs.

steps.title: This board: five stages
steps.body: Cortex-A7, 32-bit Armv7-A, 512 MiB of DDR3. The DDR driver is inside BL2 and OP-TEE is the monitor, so the chain is ROM, BL2, OP-TEE, U-Boot, Linux.

steps.title: No BL31 here
steps.body: On the 64-bit chip TF-A keeps a resident monitor (BL31) at EL3. On this 32-bit chip OP-TEE handles `smc` and PSCI itself.

steps.title: The 64-bit sibling
steps.body: Cortex-A35, ARMv8-A, 4 GiB of LPDDR4. It needs ST's DDR training firmware and has a resident BL31; its SCMI server serves clocks and resets only.

steps.title: What is the same: the SD image
steps.body: Both use a GPT, rootless assembly, a FIP found by type GUID and `extlinux.conf` on the bootable partition. A reader who knows one image layout knows the other.

steps.title: The partition names differ
steps.body: The ROM looks for `fsbl1` and `fsbl2` on this chip and `fsbla1` and `fsbla2` on the 64-bit one. The names are contracts with the silicon, so neither board may rename them.

steps.title: The SCMI server differs
steps.body: OP-TEE's own server on this chip serves clocks, resets and voltage domains; the 64-bit chip uses Arm's SCP-firmware inside OP-TEE, which at the pinned version serves clocks and resets only.

steps.title: The consequence for the SD card
steps.body: Here the card's supply is a served voltage domain, so the stock kernel device tree boots. On the 64-bit board a patched tree with fixed regulators is booted instead.

steps.title: The userland must match the CPU
steps.body: Debian `armhf` or Alpine `armv7` here, `arm64` or `aarch64` on the other board. A 64-bit rootfs does not run on this kernel. Building the Debian image needs an emulator (qemu) on any PC that cannot run 32-bit ARM code.

steps.title: Same releases, same discipline
steps.body: Both boards use TF-A 2.15.0, OP-TEE 4.11.0, U-Boot 2026.07 and Linux 6.18.58, pinned by commit or checksum.
